```plato
//==
// # Lattices
//
// Periodic cellular structures: the strut-and-node scaffolds used for additive
// manufacturing infill, metamaterials and lightweighting, and the triply
// periodic minimal surfaces that are their implicit counterpart
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice_material).
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Unit cells
//  - Lattice instances
//  - Strut distance fields
//  - Triply periodic minimal surfaces

//==
// # Unit cells
//
// A unit cell is a graph in NORMALIZED CELL COORDINATES: node positions live in
// the unit cube [0, 1]^3, so one cell description serves every cell size. The
// named standard cells and the tiling that places them in world space are in
// `lattices.library.plato`.
//
// Periodicity is a precondition, not a check. A cell is well formed for tiling
// when its node set and its strut set survive translation by one cell: a node
// with a coordinate of 1 has a twin with that coordinate 0 and the others
// unchanged, and likewise for struts lying in a face. Every cell in
// `lattices.library.plato` satisfies it. A cell that does not will tile with
// gaps or with doubled struts on the shared faces.
//
// Face coordinates are written as exact 0 and 1 literals, which is what lets the
// tiling recognize a face by comparison rather than by tolerance.

// One strut of a unit cell: an undirected pair of positions in the cell's Nodes
// array. A and B index that array; order carries no meaning, and a strut with
// A equal to B is degenerate.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Typed indices.
type LatticeStrut
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    A: ItemIndex;
    B: ItemIndex;
}
```
